11-253.r: Mid-day Meal (now PM POSHAN) → financed and managed by Ministry of HRD (now Education); Centre:State 60:40, 90:10 for NE and 3 Himalayan States, 100% for UTs without legislature.

11-254.r: Mid-day Meal (NP-NSPE) → started 15 August 1995 in 2408 blocks, including Uttar Pradesh; all blocks by 1997-98; now 'PM POSHAN'.

11-255.r: Mid-day Meal is organized by School Management, Panchayati Raj Institutions and Self Help Groups; not by contractors.

11-256.r: Akshay Patra Foundation (2000, Bengaluru) → NGO running Mid-day Meals in Government and aided schools to end classroom hunger.

11-257.r: Adamya Chetna Trust, Havells, Hindustan Zinc, DSCL Kota (Shriram Group) → corporate trusts supporting the Mid-Day Meal Programme.

11-258.r: 'School Chalo Abhiyan' (Go to School Campaign) → Uttar Pradesh, July 2000, primary education for all children aged 6-14.

11-259.r: Kalp Yojana → U.P. Government's primary education plan, started 1998.

11-261.r: Shiksha Mitra Scheme (U.P., 2000-01) → village youth teach in their own village; keeps teacher-student ratio; universalizes primary education. Both true, R not the explanation.

11-262.r: District Primary Education Programme (DPEP) → 1994; revitalize primary education; universal access, retention, better learning, less disparity among social groups.

11-263.r: Prarambhik Shiksha Kosh (October 2005) → non-lapsable fund for elementary education that receives the Education Cess (Finance Act, 2004).

11-264.r: Operation Black Board (1987) → minimum essential facilities in all primary schools.

11-265.r: Inclusive Education for Disabled at Secondary Stage (IEDSS, 2009-10) → disabled students of classes 9 to 12; replaced IEDC; subsumed in RMSA since 2013.

11-266.r: Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan → 2001; Sakshar Bharat Mission → 2009; Operation Black Board → 1987; National Literacy Mission → 1988.

11-267.r: Andragogy → methods and principles of adult education.
11-267.t: Don't confuse andragogy (teaching adults) with pedagogy (teaching children).

11-268.r: RUDSET (Rural Development and Self Employment Training) Institute → skills and entrepreneurship training for unemployed rural youth to set up their own enterprises.

11-269.r: 'Roshni' (2013, Ministry of Rural Development) → placement-linked skill training for rural/tribal youth in Left Wing Extremism affected districts.

11-270.r: PM's New 15 Point Programme for Welfare of Minorities → announced on Independence Day 2005, revised programme in 2006.

11-271.r: Nalanda Project (4 March 2014) → Ministry of Minority Affairs; faculty development for minority higher education institutions, taken up at Aligarh Muslim University.

11-272.r: MPLADS (3 December 1993) → durable community assets (health, education, sanitation, roads, water); a set share must benefit SC/ST populations; unused funds do carry forward.

11-273.r: Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana → launched 11 October 2014, birth anniversary of Jayaprakash Narayan; MPs develop model villages.

11-274.r: 1981 → International Year of Disabled; 2023 → International Year of Millets; 2024 → International Year of Camelids.

11-275.r: World Literacy Day → 8 September every year.

11-276.r: International Women's Day → 8 March every year.

11-277.r: Samajik Adhikarita Smriti Divas → 20 March every year.

11-278.r: World Consumer Rights Day → 15 March every year.

11-279.r: Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act → enacted 1976 but in force from 25 October 1975.
11-279.t: Passed in 1976, effective from 1975; both years appear as answers.

11-281.r: Rapid social change in India → modern science and technology, social planning, population growth and physical prosperity (all four).
11-281.c: Book gives no single answer: it counts all four as causes of rapid social change, and no option lists all four.

11-282.r: Kurukshetra → monthly magazine on rural development, by Publications Division (Ministry of I&B), since 1952.

11-283.r: Planning Commission expert panel (August 2011) → health surcharge on taxable income to give free health care to all.

11-284.r: National Children's Fund → 1979 (International Year of the Child); corpus Rs. one lakh under the Charitable Endowment Act, 1890.

11-285.r: National Institute of Rural Development and Panchayati Raj → Hyderabad (Telangana); autonomous body under the Ministry of Rural Development.

11-286.r: CAPART (Council for Advancement of People's Action and Rural Technology, 1 September 1986) → under Ministry of Rural Development, New Delhi; aids and evaluates rural welfare projects.

11-288.r: Aadhaar → 12-digit identity number issued by UIDAI to all residents of India; proof of identity and address.

11-290.r: Aadhaar launched 29 September 2010 from Tembhli village, Nandurbar district (Maharashtra), the first 'Aadhaar gaon'.

11-292.r: 'Vision 2020 for India' → economic development document under Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, to make India a developed country.

11-293.r: PURA (Providing Urban Amenities to Rural Areas) → model by Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, explained on the eve of the 54th Republic Day, 2003.

11-296.r: PM's Shram Awards (Ministry of Labour) → workers of Central/State PSUs and departmental undertakings, and private units employing 500 or more workers.

11-297.r: National Rehabilitation and Resettlement Policy, 2007 → covers displacement by land acquisition or any other involuntary cause; made by Ministry of Rural Development. Both statements wrong.

11-298.r: National Handicapped (now Divyangjan) Finance and Development Corporation → January 1997, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment; finances income-generating activities of disabled persons.

11-299.r: National Institute for the Visually Handicapped (now for Empowerment of Persons with Visual Disabilities) → Dehradun; under DEPwD, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

11-300.r: First university only for the disabled → Chitrakoot (U.P.), 2001; now Jagadguru Rambhadracharya Divyang State University.

11-301.r: First Open University → Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Open University, Hyderabad (then Andhra Pradesh), August 1982.

11-302.r: Tarun Bharat Sangh → NGO in Rajasthan founded by Dr. Rajendra Singh; works for sustainable development.

11-303.r: National Youth Policy 2014 (approved 9 January 2014, replaced NYP 2003) → youth aged 15-29; five objectives, 11 priority areas.

12-001.r: Types of poverty → absolute and relative (by threshold), objective and subjective (by data), transversal and persistent (by duration); 'functional poverty' is not a type.

12-002.r: UNO adopted absolute poverty definition → 1995: severe deprivation of basic needs (food, water, sanitation, health, shelter, education, information); World Bank line US $2.15 (September 2022).

12-003.r: Poverty estimation in India has used head count ratio, calorie intake and household consumption expenditure (current method, Tendulkar Committee 2005-2009); not per capita income.

12-004.r: Poverty estimates in India → based on household consumption expenditure (NSSO survey), not income, since incomes of self-employed and daily wagers are hard to measure.

12-009.r: State poverty lines updated with → CPI for Industrial Workers (CPI-IW) in urban areas; CPI for Agricultural Labourers (CPI-AL) in rural areas.
12-009.t: Don't swap: IW → urban, AL → rural.

12-010.r: 61st NSS Round (2004-05) → two consumption distributions: Uniform Recall (30-day recall, all items) and Mixed Recall (365-day for five infrequent non-food items).

12-011.r: Literacy → not used to fix the poverty line; per capita income, calorie intake and head count ratio are used.

12-012.r: Alagh Committee (task force 1977, report 1979) → poverty line based only on nutritional (calorie) needs and the related consumption expenditure.

12-013.r: Alagh task force (1979) → poverty line = spending to get 2400 kcal per person per day in rural areas and 2100 kcal in urban areas.
12-013.h: Rural work is harder, so more calories: 2400 rural, 2100 urban.

12-017.r: Tendulkar Committee (set up 2005, report 2009) → new standards to estimate population below poverty line; moved away from calorie norms.
